transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in today. What brings you here — is there something specific you’d like to talk about or get help with?

Hi, yeah, thank you. I came in because... well, my mind is just constantly jumping from one thing to another. I work in a lab, and I keep stressing over whether our new partnership is going to end up cutting my position. But then it just jumps to whether my data are wrong, or how my bills are going to pile up. And then I start worrying that my family thinks I'm falling behind, or... or whether I've already completely ruined my chances at getting into grad school. It's just a constant stream of that every day, and I really need some help getting it to stop.
Do you feel like your worrying is excessive or hard to control, even when you try to focus on something else?

Yeah, it's definitely hard to control. I try to tell myself to just focus on one task, like finishing a report or checking an assay at the lab. But... one worry just sets off another. Pretty soon I'm just staring at the screen, and my head is running through every possible way things could go wrong. I just can't seem to turn it off.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like restlessness, feeling on edge, fatigue, or muscle tension, especially when you're worrying?

Yeah, definitely. At work, I just feel... wound up, I guess. Like I can't even settle into my chair. I end up tapping my foot constantly or checking my messages over and over. Sometimes I'll just get up and walk back to the instrument room for no real reason, just because I can't sit still. And I'm so on edge that normal lab noises, like a centrifuge finishing or someone dropping a beaker, will actually startle me. It's just this constant tension.
In addition to the worry and tension you've described, have you noticed any days where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, like work or hobbies?

No, not really. I mean, I'm stressed all the time, and that's exhausting, but I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or down like that. And I still care about my work and getting into grad school—that's actually what I'm worrying about most of the time. I haven't really lost interest in things, I just can't enjoy them because my mind won't stop racing.
